subject: Arbiter Systems — VPC hosting carveout & upfront credit approval
messages:
From: Sasha Ivanov <sasha.ivanov@arbiter.ai>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurements <procurements@arbiter.ai>
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Hosting requirements & commercial ask for Arbiter pilot

Hi Rohan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency profile. We are trying to firm up procurement priorities so we can kick off a limited private deployment pilot in November. Two asks from our security and finance teams: 

1) Data residency: Arbiter needs all inference logs and customer data to remain in the us-east-1 region and for the VPC deployment to be locked to our account.
2) Audit window: our security team requires on-site-style audit evidence for a 14-day window, including access to audit logs and the right to conduct a vendor security review (read-only).
3) Upfront commercial request: to justify the pilot capex internally, they are asking for an upfront credit equal to 20% of the first 12 months' committed spend (applied to invoices as a credit).

We know these are non-standard. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accommodate the VPC carveout and the audit window, and whether the credit is something you can bring to your leadership for approval? I can share a condensed term sheet and the SOC2 summary if helpful.

Thanks,
Sasha
Head of Cloud Integrations
Arbiter Systems

--

Marissa / Laura — forwarding a brief from Arbiter. Summary of the asks: VPC bound to Arbiter's account in us-east-1; 14-day audit access window (read-only logs); and they want a 20% upfront credit against first year committed spend.

Quick context: Arbiter is a late-seed AI infra company; pilot expected to be modest (single-digit GPU capacity) but strategic for our partner program. They move fast and have an internal procurement date of Oct 20.

Marissa — can Deal Desk model the unit economics on a 20% upfront credit + the expected revenue, and flag any SLA or capacity risks?
Laura — if approved, we will need a carveout on the standard VPC hosting terms (audit access + residency lock). Jordan, loop in legal/ops for the access guardrails if this goes to approval.

I attached their term sheet & SOC2 summary.

Thanks,
Rohan

Subject: RE: Fwd: Hosting requirements & commercial ask for Arbiter pilot

Thanks for the context, Rohan. I ran a quick economic model. If Arbiter commits to a 12-month minimum of $120k ARR (baseline for the pilot scaling to prod), a 20% upfront credit equals $24k applied across the first 3 invoices. Key points from deal desk: 

- Economics: With our standard gross margin targets, the credit is acceptable if we secure a 12-month commit and standard overage pricing applies after pilot burst.
- Risk: The primary program risk is the audit access window. That can create operational overhead; we need legal to carve out explicit read-only access, a bounded list of log types, and no direct file-level access to customer data.
- Sizing: Pilot expected < 500 concurrent tokens/sec; we can assign a small dedicated pool.

Jordan — can Legal draft narrow language for the audit window (timebox + scope + contact protocol)? Laura, if you are comfortable with conditional approval (12-month commit + legal guardrails + Ops runbook signoff + logging SLAs), we can accept the credit.

I recommend the following approvals:
1) Commercial: Deal Desk approves 20% upfront credit conditioned on 12-month commit (Deal ID: DEAL-AR-8921).
2) Policy: Exec signoff to allow a VPC carveout in us-east-1 limited to the pilot and reversible on renewal.
3) Operations: Pre-launch checklist and runbook signoff by Infra within 2 weeks.

Jordan — I'll upload suggested redlines to the HubSpot deal.

-Marissa
Sr. Deal Desk Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosting requirements & commercial ask for Arbiter pilot

Thanks team — I reviewed the economics and the proposed controls. I will provide conditional executive approval on the following basis: 

1) Commercial: Approve the 20% upfront credit conditioned on a signed 12-month commitment and the credit amortized over the first three invoices.
2) Residency/Hosting: Approve a one-time VPC binding to Arbiter's account in us-east-1 for the pilot, explicitly timeboxed to the 12-month term. Any extension requires fresh exec signoff.
3) Audit access: Approve a 14-day audit window with read-only access to logs. Legal to include: (a) enumerated log sets (API, inference request traces, infra metrics), (b) access via a dedicated read-only S3 export + temporary signed URLs, (c) on-site review replaced by remote evidence unless mutually agreed. No customer plaintext data or model weights will be exposed.
4) Ops guardrails: Infra must complete a pre-launch runbook and a temporary alerting profile for the audit window. No priority support SLAs change.

Jordan — please prepare the redline language and an Ops checklist. Marissa — proceed with conditional commercial paperwork and update HubSpot. Rohan — you may share the above with Arbiter with the caveat that legal redlines are pending.

Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
